rationale:
structural: The only clause in `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outgoing_edges.fn` is "Criterion code uses {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.outgoing_edges` for this operation." It makes one structural demand. Criterion code must get edges through the `ValidationContext::outgoing_edges` method, with the signature the cited requirement declares. A criterion that bypassed it would break the clause. For example, it could call `graph.outgoing_edges` on the domain directly and so skip the dependency recording. Nothing else in the text is structural.

The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#2/fn[outgoing_edges]` provides that interface. Its declaration matches the cited signature: `&self`, `node: &NodeId<D>`, `label: D::EdgeLabel`, a return type of `Result<Snapshot<Vec<NodeId<D>>>, D::Error>`, and the `where D::EdgeLabel: PartialEq` bound. In the same function, `prepare_edges` reads the edges and computes the fingerprint, and `observe_edges` records the selection. Both are reached from the marked root, so they need no marker of their own.

The same file shows a caller going through the context method. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#1/fn[successors]` calls `self.outgoing_edges(...)`. I found no other implementation root that needs a reference. The behavioral obligations (target IDs, fingerprint, recorded dependency) belong to the cited and sibling requirements, not to this one.
